title: Structured outputs are now generally available in the Responses API
summary: Structured outputs move from beta to GA with strict JSON schema validation, lower latency and no extra cost.
content:
SAMPLE FIXTURE - synthetic data for local dry-runs, not real news.

Structured outputs are now generally available in the Responses API. Developers can pass a JSON Schema with strict: true and the model is constrained to produce conforming output. During the beta, schema violations were the top source of retries for agent pipelines.

What changed:
- Strict schema mode is GA and covered by the standard availability SLA.
- Median added latency drops from 340 ms to 120 ms.
- No additional per-token charge; pricing is unchanged.
- Nested arrays up to depth 5 are supported (previously 3).

Migration: the beta header is no longer required and will be ignored after November 1. Existing requests keep working.

title: A connector registry for the Model Context Protocol
summary: MCP gains a public connector registry with signed manifests and capability scopes.
content:
SAMPLE FIXTURE - synthetic data for local dry-runs, not real news.

The Model Context Protocol now has a public connector registry. Each entry ships a signed manifest that declares the tools it exposes, the scopes it requests and the transport it supports.

What changed:
- Connectors are discoverable by name instead of a hand-copied JSON config.
- Manifests are signed; clients can refuse unsigned connectors.
- Capability scopes (read, write, network) are declared up front, so a client can deny network access to a filesystem connector.

For builders: the registry client is in the reference SDKs behind a feature flag. Self-hosting a private registry is supported for internal tools.

Highlights:
- Hybrid KV cache offload to host RAM, raising the usable context on a single 24 GB GPU from 32k to 128k tokens for a 7B model.
- Prefix caching is enabled by default; disable with --no-enable-prefix-caching.
- Breaking change: SamplingParams.max_tokens replaces SamplingParams.max_new_tokens. The old name raises a DeprecationWarning and will be removed in 1.0.
- Measured throughput on A100 80GB with Llama-3-8B: 3,180 output tok/s at batch 64, up from 2,410.

Upgrade notes: pip install -U vllm. Configuration files using max_new_tokens need to be updated.

title: A benchmark for long-horizon agent reliability
summary: New open benchmark measures whether agents can keep a 200-step task on track without human intervention.
content:
SAMPLE FIXTURE - synthetic data for local dry-runs, not real news.

We are releasing an open benchmark for long-horizon agent reliability. Tasks require 120 to 220 tool calls and are scored on completion, recoverability after an injected failure, and cost.

What changed: existing agent benchmarks mostly measure single-shot tool use. This one injects deterministic failures (timeouts, stale data, permission errors) at fixed steps and measures whether the agent notices and recovers.

Baseline results: the strongest configuration completes 41% of tasks unaided; adding an explicit retry policy raises it to 58%. Code and task definitions are Apache 2.0.

Structured outputs are now generally available in the Responses API, and the same idea is available in open serving stacks through grammar-constrained decoding. We compare strict JSON schema enforcement across three runtimes and look at the latency cost of constrained decoding.

title: Retrieval Compression for Long-Context Agents
summary: Abstract: We show that compressing retrieved passages into learned summary tokens preserves 94% of downstream task accuracy while cutting prompt tokens by 6x.
content:
SAMPLE FIXTURE - synthetic data for local dry-runs, not real news.

Abstract:
We study retrieval compression for long-context agents. Retrieved passages are encoded into learned summary tokens before being placed in the prompt. Across five agentic benchmarks, the method preserves 94% of task accuracy relative to full-text retrieval while reducing prompt tokens by 6x and end-to-end latency by 2.3x. We release training code and the compression checkpoints.
